Amir / Kimberly — pulled together an initial sizing note (see inline). I also uploaded a short text export (sizing_notes_20261102.txt). High-level summary first, then the math.

Summary / recommendation:
- Recommended reserved pool: 8 dedicated H100-80GB pods (pod = single GPU node in this proposal) with 2 hot-standby pods for failover (total commit = 10).
  - 70B variant (int8): place on 6 pods (primary serving capacity). Each pod holds one 70B int8 copy w/ KV cache for 32k context.
  - 7B variant (int8): place on 2 pods (for lower-cost routing and bulk inference).
- Rationale: a single H100-80GB with int8 quant fits a 70B model with KV cache for 32k context when using per-pod KV sharding and optimized kernel packing; int8 reduces base weight footprint close to ~70GB. We keep two additional pods as buffer for rolling updates and burst headroom.
- Fallbacks: route to 7B-quant with quality-aware routing for best-effort requests; implement graceful degradation policy in the routing layer with a soft threshold at 85% utilization.

Sizing math and assumptions (simplified):
- Weight footprint: 70B fp16 ~ 140GB (theoretical); int8 quant reduces storage by ~2x -> ~70GB resident on device with optimized packing and kernel fusion. (Note: exact size depends on quantization scheme; we validated the candidate ~int8 build in our staging cluster.)
- KV cache overhead: for transformers, KV cache scales roughly linearly with context tokens. For our template we estimate ~0.00068 GB per token for the 70B layout (this includes keys+values and some allocator overhead).
  - For 32k context: 32,768 tokens * 0.00068 GB/token ~= 22.3 GB KV cache per active sequence.
- Working memory and activation peaks: we budget 4–6 GB for activations and temporary buffers during decoding at peak batch sizes.
- Total per-pod resident memory (weights + KV + working buffers): ~70 GB + 22.3 GB + 6 GB ~= 98.3 GB. This exceeds a single 80GB device, so we rely on two implementation options:
  1) Int8 single-device fit by leveraging kernel-level offloading of select tensors to host pinned memory with NVMe staging (adds ~20–60ms added generation latency depending on access pattern). Not ideal for latency-sensitive interactive flows.
  2) Model-sharded approach across NVLink-connected GPUs (2x H100-80GB) — we can run a 70B fp16/int8 instance across two GPUs with near-linear memory aggregation and less offload penalty.

Given MediCore's latency requirements for interactive sessions, we recommend option (2) for critical capacity: deploy the 70B as a 2x-GPU sharded pod type (we count each pair as one logical serving unit in the SOW). Practically, the reserved pool above maps to:
- 6 logical 70B serving units implemented as 12 physical H100-80GB GPUs (i.e., 6 pairs) + 2 logical spare units (4 GPUs) = 16 physical GPUs in the reserved pool for 70B.
- 7B instances are single-GPU and very lightweight when int8 quantized (~4–6 GB weights resident + small KV cache for shorter contexts). We recommend 2 single-GPU pods for the 7B variant (2 H100-80GB GPUs).

Throughput roughs (for planning):
- One 70B logical unit (2x H100 pair) can handle ~5–6 concurrent decoding sessions at our target batching settings (dynamic batches up to 16 for throughput cases) with p95 latency in the 400–700ms range for short to medium responses.
- To reach the 30 concurrent sessions target during peak: 30 / 5 = 6 logical 70B units. Add 25% headroom -> 7.5 -> round to 8 logical units -> matches the 6 + 2 spare in recommendation above when you include 7B routing for lower quality fallbacks.

Operational notes / SOW language to include:
- Physical commitment: 16 H100-80GB GPUs dedicated to 70B logical units + 2 H100-80GB GPUs for 7B (total 18 GPUs), with optional burst access to additional pooled capacity if needed.
- Canary & rollout: we recommend one canary logical unit (a single 2x GPU pair) before full traffic migration to monitor latency for long-context samples.
- Quantization caveat: int8 quant is validated for general RAG workloads; expect <1.0% delta in key eval metrics vs fp16 in our internal tests. If MediCore requires bit-for-bit deterministic outputs, specify fp16 in SOW and we will increase the reserved GPU counts accordingly.

I'll add a short appendix to the draft SOW explaining the mapping from logical serving units to physical GPUs so procurement can see "units -> GPUs" immediately.

Adding ops perspective and autoscaling notes.

- Autoscaling: because this is a reserved capacity deal, we suggest a two-layer policy: (A) reserved floor that keeps all logical units warm for the peak SLA, (B) burst pool in the shared tenancy that can be claimed for short-duration experiments (billing extra). This prevents noisy neighbors and cold-starts for production traffic.
- Network & IO: for 2x-GPU sharded pods, ensure NVLink topology and driver versions are specified in the deployment manifest — we will include required host images in the SOW appendix.
- Monitoring: include tracing keys and token-level cost-export in the SOW so MediCore can map dollars to routes. We'll add an SLA clause for p95 latency spikes tied to specific maintenance windows.

Operational recommendation: commit to 8 logical 70B units (i.e., 16 GPUs) + 2 single-GPU 7B pods in SOW, but bill the first month with an "early-termination flexibility" clause (30-day notice) if pilot metrics force a reshape. This helps the customer mitigate risk when they switch to aggressive production.
